one_liner: Rust open UDP BitTorrent tracker (BEP 15) whose io_uring backend out-serves its own epoll path and opentracker.
what_it_does: aquatic_udp is a standalone tracker daemon that answers BEP 15 connect/announce/scrape requests over UDP. It keeps all swarm state in memory (no database) and is configured through a generated TOML file. It supports IPv4 and IPv6 on separate sockets, info-hash allow/deny lists reloaded on SIGUSR1, Prometheus metrics and optional full-scrape exports. It replaces opentracker or chihaya as a process that clients reach at udp://host:port; it is not an event-loop library, and its io_uring code is internal (the lib crate exposes little more than run(Config)).
how_it_is_fast: N socket-worker threads each bind their own SO_REUSEPORT UDP socket (SO_REUSEPORT_LB on FreeBSD), so the kernel spreads packets across them and each request is handled to completion on the thread that received it. Swarm state is split into 16 parking_lot RwLock shards per IP version, and announces take an upgradable read lock so writes are brief. Torrents with 2 or fewer peers are stored inline in an ArrayVec with no heap allocation, and connection IDs are stateless keyed-BLAKE3 MACs instead of a connection table. The opt-in io_uring backend uses multishot RecvMsgMulti with a provided-buffer ring (buf_ring), registered file descriptors, batched SendMsg entries and a COOP_TASKRUN/SINGLE_ISSUER ring, which replaces the default mio/epoll path's per-packet recv/send syscalls with one submit_and_wait per batch.
when_to_use: You run a public or high-traffic open UDP tracker on Linux and opentracker is the incumbent: in the maintainer's benchmark the io_uring build answered 1.19x to 1.37x more requests per second than opentracker at 1 to 16 cores.
Your kernel is Linux 6.0 or later and you can build with --features io-uring, which gained about 1.1x to 1.2x over the default epoll build at 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 16 cores.
You need to scale one tracker across many cores: the benchmark went from 226k responses/s at 1 core to 1.52M at 8 and 2.26M at 16.
You want Prometheus metrics, access lists, IPv4 plus IPv6 and scrape-statistics exports built in, without running a database.
when_not_to_use: You want a general event loop or async I/O library: this is a tracker application, and the io_uring machinery is not a reusable API.

You run a private tracker: there are no passkeys or per-user accounting (issue #214 is still an open discussion), download counts are always reported as 0, and the IP a client puts in its announce is ignored in favour of the packet's source IP.

You are on a pre-6.0 kernel or not on Linux: the io-uring feature fails to compile off Linux and fails a runtime probe on old kernels, which leaves the mio/epoll build. On the benchmark page that build was about 0.98x opentracker at 1, 2 and 4 cores and pulled ahead only from 6 cores.

You track very large swarms on constrained RAM: one unverified user report (issue #257, closed by its author six minutes after filing, with no maintainer reply) claims about 100k QPS and 13 GB RAM for aquatic against 800k QPS and 5 GB for opentracker at 50M peers on dual Xeon E5-2650 v2. The published benchmark simulated only 2M peers over loopback.
You need numbers that match the current code: the benchmark is from February 2024 (commit 21a5301), the torrent-map structures were reworked in May 2026, and the benchmark has not been rerun since.

integration.form: crate (mainly the standalone aquatic_udp binary; a lib target exposes config and run)
integration.dependencies: mio, socket2, parking_lot, hashbrown, crossbeam-channel, blake3, arrayvec, aquatic_udp_protocol (zerocopy); default features add mimalloc (needs cmake and a C compiler) and metrics/Prometheus; optional io-uring crate behind the io-uring feature
integration.min_toolchain: Rust stable (README recommends the latest; master declares no rust-version; the crates.io 0.9.0 release declares 1.64). The io-uring feature needs Linux 6.0+.
integration.platforms: Unix-like: Linux (CI builds and tests, including with io-uring), macOS (CI build only), FreeBSD (SO_REUSEPORT_LB handling). The io_uring backend is Linux 6.0+ only. Any CPU architecture; the README recommends target-cpu=native without AVX-512.
integration.thread_safety: Not applicable as a library. Internally, socket workers share swarm state through RwLock shards, and each io_uring ring is thread-local and single-issuer.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — it can replace opentracker as a server with no client-side change (same BEP 15 protocol), but the config format differs. Against epoll it is not an API replacement; io_uring vs epoll is a build feature plus a config flag inside aquatic itself.

gotchas: The default config sets socket_workers = 1. Set it to 0 (one per available vCPU) or to an explicit N, or you get single-core throughput.

io_uring requires both the cargo feature io-uring and network.use_io_uring (which defaults to true once the feature is compiled in). Kernel support is detected by probing for SendZc as a proxy for Linux 6.0, and ring submit errors are unwrapped, so they panic; since 0.9.0 any worker panic stops the whole process.

The io_uring backend is marked experimental. The 0.9.0 changelog lists 'Fix io_uring UB issues', the TODO notes that it has not yet run cleanly under valgrind or AddressSanitizer, and its unsafe buf_ring code is copied from a tokio-uring fork.

The default 8 MB socket receive buffer only takes effect if net.core.rmem_max allows it (the config docs call this a big factor in dropped packets). Master also carries unreleased breaking config changes (separate address_ipv4/address_ipv6) that differ from the 0.9.0 release.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick aquatic when you need a finished UDP tracker rather than a runtime to build one: monoio, libhv and PhotonLibOS are general-purpose I/O frameworks, and io_uring-echo-server is a TCP echo demo. Its io_uring-over-epoll gain (about 1.1-1.2x, measured on UDP inside one codebase) is smaller than monoio's 1.86x or the echo server's 1.4x on TCP ping-pong.
verified_claims_summary: The maintainer's aquatic_bencher (February 2024, commit 21a5301) drove loopback IPv4 UDP traffic from a load generator simulating 1M torrents and 2M peers, with about 100 announces per scrape, and pinned tracker and generator to CPUs with taskset on a Hetzner CCX63 (AMD EPYC 7003 Milan, 48 vCPUs, Linux 6.5.10). aquatic was built with rustc 1.76, thin LTO and target-cpu=native without AVX-512; opentracker was built with GCC 12.2 -O3 -march=native and ran N blocking-recvfrom worker threads. At 1 core the io_uring build served 226k responses/s against 187k for the mio (epoll) build and 191k for opentracker; at 16 cores it served 2.26M against 2.04M and 1.65M, and at 12 cores the mio build edged ahead.
status_note: Actively maintained by its author (last commit 2026-07-13) under Apache-2.0, and described as production-ready (explodie.org runs it at about 100k req/s), but the last tagged and crates.io release is 0.9.0 from 2024, so current fixes mean building from master.
